facts.fact: (a) Port Moresby is the capital and largest city of Papua New Guinea, on the Coral Sea at the south-western end of the Papuan Peninsula; Wikipedia gives 364,145 inhabitants at the 2011 census and 756,754 at the 2024 census (Wikivoyage still quotes about 365,000, 2011).
(a) The original Motu-Koitabu settlement at the site (Hanuabada, five villages) is still there; Captain John Moresby named the harbour in 1873 for his father, Fairfax Moresby.

(a) Role: Wikivoyage calls it the gateway to PNG ('almost all visitors to the country pass through the city') but says it has few attractions and 'is usually just a stopping off point for tourists heading to other parts of PNG'. The tourism authority calls it the country's administrative and economic centre and main point of entry.

(a) Distinctive fact: with average yearly rainfall of 898.8 mm it is the driest place in New Guinea (Wikipedia). The Hiri Moale Festival centres on a race of up to 100 traditional lakatoi canoes leaving Ela Beach (Wikivoyage).

(a) Sights listed by Wikivoyage: Port Moresby Nature Park (birds of paradise, cassowaries; formerly the National Capital Botanical Gardens), PNG National Museum & Art Gallery (Waigani; Mon-Sat 9AM-3PM, Sun 1-3PM; no photography inside), Bomana War Cemetery (3,824 Commonwealth WWII burials; 9AM-4PM; free), Parliament Haus (usually open, free), Touaguba Hill view, Moitaka Wildlife Sanctuary (crocodiles).

(b) Arrival: Jacksons International Airport (POM), 8 km out, is PNG's main international airport; Air Niugini flies from Cairns, Sydney, Brisbane, Singapore, Manila, Hong Kong and others, Qantas from Brisbane, PNG Air from Cairns, Solomon Airlines from Honiara, Citilink from Denpasar. International terminal has an ATM and money changer; domestic terminal is a 300 m walk and has no air conditioning.

(b) Airport to town: hotels provide transfers; Wikivoyage says a bus takes 30 minutes and taxis about 20 minutes for 80 PGK. The tourism authority gives 15-20 minutes by taxi, hotel transfer or hire car and lists direct flights from Brisbane, Cairns, Sydney, Manila, Singapore, Hong Kong, Guangzhou, Honiara, Nadi and Port Vila.

(b) Getting around: the city is spread out and 'there is little attraction in the CBD and walking around will not get you very far'; Wikivoyage says you will be reliant on motorised transport. Taxis rarely use meters, so agree the fare first: short trips K10-20, Waigani to Ela Beach K40-50, airport K50-100. Wikivoyage calls organising transport through your hotel 'the easiest and safest way'. PMV minibuses are cheap and cover the city.

(b) Hire cars: available near the airport, but Wikivoyage warns of stone-throwing at cars in some areas, and that outside the city roads become muddy trails needing a 4x4 with an experienced driver (Sogeri, Kokoda start). Traffic drives on the left.

(b) Domestic hub: Air Niugini connects Port Moresby with most provincial capitals; there are no major roads from Port Moresby to elsewhere beyond the near hinterland and a coastal road southeast. The tourism authority lists domestic flights to Lae, Rabaul, Mount Hagen, Madang and Wewak.

(c) Wikivoyage 'Stay safe', verbatim: 'Port Moresby is well known for its crime. Carjackings, muggings and worse are common. Women are particularly at risk. Foreigners are sometimes specifically targeted. As such, it has been rated as one of the least livable cities in the world.'

(c) Wikivoyage also says: police officers have been found complicit in major crime; the Waigani area, 'particularly the area around the traffic lights and the Port Moresby Golf Club', has had numerous carjackings; the Morata district is known for weekend riots; 'It's best to not walk between locations in Port Moresby, or travel at night'; seek advice from someone familiar with the city before entering unknown areas.

(c) Wikivoyage balances this: 'the local people are mainly friendly and peaceful. The main risks are from idle young people, mostly having fun and struggling for money.' It also notes the traditional 'pay back' concept can be 'wild and violent'. Saltwater crocodiles are common across PNG but 'you are extremely unlikely to run into one'; the golf course water holes hold crocodiles.

(c) Wikivoyage 'Sleep': due to the security situation 'it's likely that you won't leave your hotel after dark, so choose one with good dining and recreation options'. Country page: most Port Moresby hotels are 'secure and situated inside compounds, generally with guards'; 'actual gunfire in the capital is mercifully rare'; avoid going out after dark.

(c) Country-level 'Stay safe' (Wikivoyage Papua New Guinea) reproduces the US State Department advisory of 17 January 2024 (link dead): 'Reconsider travel to Papua New Guinea due to crime, civil unrest, and piracy', with increased caution for kidnapping, unexploded ordnance, healthcare gaps and natural disasters. It names raskol gangs as active in major cities, 'especially in Port Moresby and Lae'. The Highlands (except Mt Hagen and Goroka) and central Bougainville are 'do not travel' areas in that advisory; Port Moresby itself is not on that list.

(c) PNG Tourism Promotion Authority (Port Moresby page, loads): 'Avoid walking alone at night or in unfamiliar areas such as settlements or isolated roads. Stick to well-frequented places and travel with a local guide or tour operator where possible.' 'Use hotel-arranged transfers or trusted taxi services. Avoid using PMVs ... unless accompanied by a local.'

(c) Tourism authority 'Safety & Health' page: use common sense, avoid secluded areas, stay with possessions, do not walk alone at night; travelling with a local guide is advised; insurance recommended; malaria is a serious risk (start anti-malarials before arrival); ensure polio vaccination; emergency numbers Port Moresby only: Police 112, Fire 110/002, St John Ambulance 111; Medivac Pacific Services +675 323 5626.

(d) Climate (Wikipedia): tropical savanna climate (Koppen Aw) with relatively constant temperatures; 'The wet season starts in December and ends in May; the dry season covers the remaining six months' (June-November). Average highs 28 to 32 C, lows about 23 C.

(d) Country page (Wikivoyage): the '(very) wet season runs from about December to March. The best months for trekking are June to September.' No Port Moresby-specific 'best months' statement was found on Wikivoyage or the tourism site; June-November dry season is the only sourced indication.

(e) Visa: everyone needs a visa; a 60-day visa on arrival is available to EU/EFTA, UK, US, NZ, Canada, Japan and many others, 30-day to Australia, India, Russia and some others, at Port Moresby, Mount Hagen, Alotau and Tokua (Rabaul) airports only. It is not granted for stays under 8 hours, so airport transit passengers cannot leave the airport.

(e) Entry fees: National Museum is free on weekdays and K10 at weekends; Bomana War Cemetery and Parliament Haus are free (Wikivoyage, listings updated 2019). Hotels are expensive: Wikivoyage lists Airways Hotel K550-800, Holiday Inn Express about K520, Ela Beach Hotel K550+ (2017-2019 prices).

(e) Beaches and land in PNG are owned by villages, families or individuals; ask permission and a small entry fee may be payable; avoid swimming in rivers, estuaries and mangrove shores because of crocodiles (tourism authority).

(f) Tip: get the driver's phone number and call a reliable driver or your hotel rather than hailing; Wikivoyage says there is 'a genuine risk of robbery that can be avoided if the hotel knows exactly who you went with'.

(f) Tip: tell the hotel your arrival time and which terminal (international or domestic); hotel transfers are standard. Check in for Air Niugini domestic flights at the transfer desk in the international terminal if connecting.

(f) Tip: Ela Beach Craft Market runs on the last Saturday of each month for souvenirs (Wikivoyage); the tourism authority lists monthly craft markets at the Moresby Arts Theatre, National Museum, Harbourside, Vision City and others.

(f) Tip: day trips are the main draw outside the city: Varirata National Park (about 45 minutes; birdwatching incl. Raggiana bird-of-paradise), Sogeri Plateau, Loloata Island Resort (snorkelling, diving). Kokoda Track starts at Owen's Corner, an hour by bus from the city; walked by 4,000+ people a year in 6-12 days, usually in guided groups.
(f) Tip: respect: handshake greeting, avoiding direct eye contact is a sign of respect, and ask consent before photographing people.

(g) Hiri Moale Festival is on the weekend of Independence Day in mid-September (Wikivoyage) and is described as the city's main cultural show; it is the only event found that drives visitor numbers. The tourism authority's events page lists no Port Moresby date for 2026 that was confirmed.

unverified: Current Port Moresby safety status: the only US advisory text found is the 17 Jan 2024 quote on Wikivoyage (original link dead); no current government advisory was fetched.
Whether the city's population is 364k (2011) or 757k (2024) as the Wikipedia infobox figure: the 2024 figure comes from Wikipedia's text and a cite to citypopulation.de, not independently checked.
Current entry prices and opening hours for Nature Park, Bomana, Parliament Haus tours (Wikivoyage items are dated 2017-2019).
Whether PMVs are advisable: Wikivoyage describes them as cheap and used by locals, the tourism authority advises avoiding them unless accompanied by a local.
Best months specific to Port Moresby: none stated by a source; June-November dry season is Wikipedia's climate description only.
Hiri Moale Festival 2026 dates and whether it still runs on Independence Day weekend.

name: Rabaul
reasons: See Tavurvur smoke across Simpson Harbour
Watch the volcanoes from the observatory lookout
Walk into the Japanese Barge Tunnel

facts.fact: (a) Rabaul is a township on the Gazelle Peninsula in the northeast of New Britain, formerly the provincial capital and main settlement of East New Britain. A 19 September 1994 eruption of Tavurvur and Vulcan covered the town in ash, collapsed 80% of its buildings, and the provincial capital moved to Kokopo about 20 km away. Wikipedia gives its population as 17,044 in 1990 (no current figure found).

(a) Distinctive facts: the evacuation drills meant only five people died in 1994 (Wikipedia; Wikivoyage says 'a handful'). The Japanese army dug 'many kilometers of tunnels' around Rabaul that can still be seen, with about 110,000 Japanese troops based there by 1943. Rabaul means mangrove in Kuanua. Wikivoyage covers Rabaul together with Kokopo.

(a) Role for visitors (Wikivoyage): popular for scuba diving and snorkelling, a spectacular harbour, WWII history that attracts many Japanese visitors; sights listed: Mount Tavurvur and hot springs (K5, parking lot where you pay; hot springs 'deadly'), Bitapaka War Cemetery (free), Japanese Barge Tunnel (K7), General Yamamoto's Bunker (K5), New Guinea Club Museum (K5), Volcano Observatory lookout (free), Kokopo War and Cultural Museum (K10). Prices listed March 2017.

(a) Volcanic status (Wikipedia): Vulcan has been quiet since 1994; Tavurvur has small and large eruptions intermittently, the most recent of note on 29 August 2014; a government volcano observatory has watched the volcanoes since the 1950s. Wikivoyage: the city 'always runs the risk of further volcanic activity'.

(b) Arrival by air: Air Niugini flies daily from Port Moresby plus from Lae, Kavieng, Hoskins, Buka. The airport (code RAB) is at Tokua, southeast of Kokopo, because the old Rabaul airport was destroyed in 1994; Tokua has also been closed by ashfall. The tourism authority's Port Moresby page lists Rabaul among domestic flight destinations.

(b) Airport to town: hotel pickup often costs K40 or more, a taxi a similar amount, or public minibuses to Kokopo for K2; the 1A bus runs Kokopo to Rabaul in about 40 minutes for K3.50 (K5 if raining). Wikivoyage warns the airport has little seating, very hot, no water for sale, and to check in 1.5-2 hours ahead. By sea, coastal ships link Lae and Rabaul and some carry passengers.

(b) Getting around: hire cars from hotels and companies cost about K240/day plus mileage and fuel (about K400 for a Kokopo-Rabaul day trip); parts of the Kokopo-Rabaul road are damaged by mudslides and 4WD may be advisable. Hotels organise tours (war sites, volcano; diving, Duke of York Islands), 'expensive unless you have a big group - think minimum K700 per car'.

(c) The Wikivoyage Rabaul page has no 'Stay safe' section; its only safety-related wording is that the city 'always runs the risk of further volcanic activity', that the hot springs at Tavurvur are 'deadly', and that Kokopo-Rabaul road and side roads can be rough. Nothing on crime in Rabaul was found there.

(c) Wikivoyage Papua New Guinea 'Stay safe' (country level): PNG has many active volcanoes and several treks involve climbing them; 'Always heed local advice' and check volcanic activity reports. It says the raskol gang problem is 'especially in Port Moresby and Lae' and that 'villages are quite safe'. The US advisory it quotes (17 Jan 2024, link dead) says 'Reconsider travel to Papua New Guinea due to crime, civil unrest, and piracy'; Rabaul/East New Britain is not named among its do-not-travel areas.

(c) Tourism authority: use common sense, avoid secluded areas, do not walk alone at night, explore with a local guide; Ring of Fire, active volcanoes, earthquakes and tsunamis; malaria serious; check insurance covers diving; crocodiles and sharks advice; ask permission before using beaches.

(d) Climate (Wikipedia): tropical rainforest climate (Af), 'constantly hot, humid, overcast and oppressive', significant rainfall year-round, average annual temperature 26.9 C and rainfall 2,201 mm (1974-1994 data). The page gives no dry/wet months; Wikipedia adds that Tokua airport has been closed by ash driven by the northwest monsoon winds.

(d) Country-level only (Wikivoyage Papua New Guinea): 'The (very) wet season runs from about December to March. The best months for trekking are June to September.' No Rabaul-specific best months were found, so this is not asserted for Rabaul.
(e) Visa on arrival is possible at Tokua Airport (Rabaul), 60 days for EU/EFTA, UK, US, NZ, Canada, Japan and many others; 30 days for Australians; others need an advance visa.

(e) Costs per Wikivoyage (2017 prices): Tavurvur parking/entry K5, Yamamoto's Bunker K5, New Guinea Club Museum K5, Barge Tunnel K7, Kokopo museum K10; Kokopo Beach Bungalow Resort K550+. Tours via hotels from about K700 per car.

(e) Tour operators: the tourism authority lists Rabaul Historical Tours (info@rhtpng.com, +675 8174 6909 / 7115 6650, Kokopo-Rabaul Road) offering guided tours of Rabaul and Kokopo including the Volcano Observatory and war sites; its East New Britain story also lists PNG Tour Guide and Rabaul Scenic Tours. Dive operators on Wikivoyage: Kabaira Dive Rabaul (about one hour from Rabaul/Kokopo), Rabaul Kokopo Dive (Rapopo Plantation Resort).

(f) Tip: stay in Kokopo, not Rabaul; Wikivoyage's accommodation list is mostly Kokopo resorts (Rapopo Plantation, Kokopo Beach Bungalow, Kokopo Village Resort) plus the 34-room Rabaul Hotel, 45 minutes from Tokua Airport.

(f) Tip: the Tavurvur and hot-springs route is unsigned and winding (Wikivoyage gives turn-by-turn directions); the Japanese Barge Tunnel is down an unmarked rough track and its sign 'is not right at the turnoff', so a guide or driver helps.
(f) Tip: Mount Mother (Kabiu), 700 m, can be climbed early in the morning from Matalau Village; Mt Tavanabatir hosts the Volcano Observatory and gives a panorama over Rabaul town.
(f) Tip: sites on the East New Britain history list: Bita Paka War Cemetery, Montevideo Maru Memorial, Japanese War Memorial on Namanula Hill, submarine base, Namanula Hill (former German HQ).

(g) The tourism authority's events page lists the Mask & Warwagira Festival (coastal traditions, masks, maritime culture) among PNG's annual festivals; it does not state a date or location on that page, and the Rabaul link and timing were not confirmed. Wikipedia's Warwagira page was not read for dates.

unverified: Any crime or personal-safety advice specific to Rabaul or Kokopo: Wikivoyage has no Stay safe section for it and none was found elsewhere.
Current Tavurvur activity, access rules or exclusion zone, and whether climbing is currently permitted; last eruption noted by Wikipedia is 29 August 2014.
Rabaul-specific best months or dry/wet pattern: Wikipedia says rainfall is year-round; country-level wet season Dec-Mar and trekking June-Sept are not Rabaul-specific.

name: Madang
reasons: Hike to the crater on Karkar Island

facts.fact: Madang is a town in Madang Province on the north coast of Papua New Guinea; Wikivoyage gives a 2013 population of almost 30,000 and says it is 'said to be one of the prettiest towns in the South Pacific', 'pleasant and laid back' and 'likely the best place to begin your PNG visit'.

Wikipedia: Madang (old German name Friedrich-Wilhelmshafen) is the capital of Madang Province, population 27,420 (2005), one of the major towns in PNG. Captured by Japan in 1942 and retaken by Australian forces on 24 April 1944; it was virtually destroyed in the fighting and rebuilt.
Distinctive: Madang is viewed by many in PNG as safer and more pleasant for expatriates than Lae and Port Moresby, so NGOs (CUSO, VSO, Save the Children, WWF, World Vision) base offices there.

Wikivoyage: many visitors come for the 'fine Scuba diving available in nearby waters'; others for a 'pretty, small, relatively safe PNG town' to walk around. The shoreline has many small sandy swimming spots with shade.

Getting there: national airlines fly in on a regular schedule including jets; Air Niugini has daily flights from Port Moresby and flights from several other PNG centres; PNG Air flies from Mt Hagen and Wewak. By road from Lae and the major Highlands centres; slow boat from Wewak or other destinations. The airport closes at 5PM to avoid collisions with flying foxes at dusk.

Getting around: 'buses' (minivans or trucks with a bench in the back) connect nearby towns from the central bus station near the market; each vehicle shows a number for its destination and you can flag one down; they are typically crowded.

Safety (Madang page, quoted closely): 'It is almost impossible to get around Madang township after 6PM. There are no taxis, and it is not advisable to walk around the town after dark. If you need to be somewhere else for dinner or drinks (apart from your hotel), make sure you pre-arrange a driver... plan to spend most evenings at your hotel or resort.' The Madang page has no separate 'Stay safe' section.

Safety (PNG country page): the country has a reputation as risky 'primarily' in Australian circles, because of criminal gangs (raskols) in major cities, 'especially in Port Moresby and Lae'. It says 'Madang, Wewak, Goroka, Mt Hagen, and Tari are much safer', and 'The villages are quite safe as the locals will adopt you'. Advice: stay up to date on law and order for the places you plan to visit; 'Avoid going out after dark, but if you must, stay very alert'; ask your hotel about tours of any city.

Safety (PNG country page): it quotes a US State Department advisory of 17 January 2024 (link now dead): 'Reconsider travel to Papua New Guinea due to crime, civil unrest, and piracy', with 'do not travel' for central Bougainville and the Highlands except Mt Hagen and Goroka. Madang is not named in the exceptions. This is a Wikivoyage quotation of a 2024 advisory, not a current one.

Other hazards on the PNG page: saltwater crocodiles are common in coastal waters and rivers ('Avoid swimming except at higher elevations and in hotel swimming pools'); malaria is a hazard; tap water in some regions is unsafe; WHO advises a polio booster; small-plane flying is risky (Air Niugini has had one fatal accident since 1973).

Climate: tropical rainforest (Köppen Af), hot year-round, average annual high 30.6 C and low 23.8 C; 3,106.8 mm of rain a year over 224 days, 'a wetter and drier season'; wettest month April (389.4 mm), driest September (82.6 mm, 11 rain days); most sun in September, least in March.
PNG-wide climate: 'The (very) wet season runs from about December to March. The best months for trekking are June to September.' (country-wide statement, not Madang-specific).

Coastwatchers Lighthouse: Wikivoyage lists 'Coastwatchers Memorial', 'a working lighthouse on Madang Harbor' honouring the mainly Australian coastwatchers who stayed after the Japanese invasion and reported ship and plane movements with local helpers.

Madang Central Market: 'a busy local market' in the centre; people come daily from the Highlands with produce and load up with goods. Open every day except Sunday, mostly fruit and vegetables, with some bags, necklaces and t-shirts.

Krangket Island: short boat trip, boats every half hour from the small boat terminal, 5 minutes, 2 kina (Wikivoyage figure, undated); two villages, no roads; Krangket Lodge 80 kina a night (undated). Wikipedia has no Krangket Island article (404).

Karkar Island: oval volcanic island about 74 km off the north coast in Madang Province, about 25 km by 19 km, with an active volcano with two nested calderas; last eruption listed 26 February 2013 (marked citation needed); population approx. 70,000; known for the view from the mountain down to Madang.

tips.fact: Pre-arrange a driver for any evening outing; there are no taxis after dark.

Village tours can be booked through any hotel for approx. US$25 per person for an afternoon including transport; a half-day north-coast tour (WWII sites, missionary stations) is around US$40 from Madang Resort (undated figures).
Village guesthouses (Hobe, Haya) offered 25 kina a night; contact the Madang Visitor and Cultural Bureau, 852-3302 (undated, may be out of date).
Craft shops at Madang Resort and Madang Lodge are described as the best places to buy crafts and reasonably priced; the market mostly sells produce.
Madang Resort Hotel has an on-site dive shop; Jais Aben Resort caters to divers and can arrange a pickup from its jetty by the Madang Resort dive store.
North coast: an old Japanese WWII airfield now mostly covered by jungle with plane wreckage, bomb craters and a Mitsubishi 'Betty' bomber.

unverified: Current hours, entry costs and any fee for Coastwatchers Lighthouse (a memorial; no hours or price given).

Diving seasons: the Madang Wikivoyage page gives none and no dive-operator page was fetched. Only the Wikipedia rainfall (driest September, wettest April) and the country-wide wet season (about December to March, per Wikivoyage) are sourced.

Current official safety advisory: the US State Department text on Wikivoyage is dated January 2024 and its link is dead; Madang is not named in it. Check a current government advisory (e.g. DFAT, Smartraveller).
Kina prices on Wikivoyage are undated and likely out of date.
papuanewguinea.travel was not fetched (blocks scripts); no tourism-board or Madang Visitor and Cultural Bureau page was read.
Whether Krangket Island and Madang Central Market need any permit or village fee: not stated.

name: Alotau
reasons: Remember the Battle of Milne Bay

facts.fact: Alotau is the capital of Milne Bay Province, in the far south-east of PNG on the tip of the Papuan Peninsula, on the northern shore of Milne Bay. It became provincial capital in 1969, moved from Samarai. Wikivoyage calls it a 'laid-back little town' that is 'a gateway to some of the most fascinating and unspoilt islands in the world'.

Wikipedia: the area is where the invading Japanese army suffered its first land defeat in the Pacific War in 1942 (Battle of Milne Bay), before the Kokoda Track battle; a memorial park at the old battle site commemorates it. Alotau is the gateway to Milne Bay Province, 'noted for its coral reef and scuba diving experiences'.

Milne Bay Province: 14,345 km2 of land and 252,990 km2 of sea, more than 600 islands (about 160 inhabited), about 412,158 inhabitants (2024 census), about 48 languages. Its reef systems are 'some of the most biodiverse in the world'. (No Wikivoyage article 'Milne Bay Province' exists; Wikivoyage region is titled 'Milne Bay'.)

Getting there: Gurney Airport (12 km from town). Air Niugini has daily flights from Port Moresby; Airlines PNG has daily flights from Lae and Port Moresby and twice weekly links to the Trobriand Islands and Misima (Wikivoyage, undated). No passenger-only shipping; coastal freighters from Port Moresby or Lae may take you, 'be prepared for a long wait'.

Gurney Airport (Alotau) is one of only four places where a PNG visa on arrival is available (with Mount Hagen, Port Moresby, Tokua/Rabaul); visa on arrival only for stays longer than 8 hours. Everyone needs a visa; 60-day visa on arrival for many nationalities incl. UK, US, NZ, EU/EFTA (Wikivoyage; check the official eVisa/immigration site before travel).

Getting around town: 'Walk!' - Alotau is not very large. Islands are reached by boat; Wikivoyage lists Fergusson Island as 'Can only be reached by boat', Samarai as 'a short boat ride from Alotau', and says Doini Island resort is about one hour by boat.

Samarai: small island at the entrance to Milne Bay, a boom town in the 19th century with up to five hotels for gold prospectors, former provincial capital (colonial District HQ until 1969); about 20 minutes to walk round, 'a few memories of its former importance'.

Fergusson Island: 'A geothermal island. Good bird watching with a rare species of Bird of Paradise and the Curl Crested Manucode.' Normanby and Goodenough: 'Totally unspoilt islands for exploring, bird watching, etc. Very limited accommodation.' D'Entrecasteaux Islands (Goodenough, Fergusson, Sanaroa, Dobu, Normanby) still have volcanic activity, especially around Dobu and Fergusson.

Trobriand Islands: 'Islands of Love'; part of the Kula Ring; population about 12,000, mostly on Kiriwina; PNG Air two flights weekly from Port Moresby via Alotau on a small Twin Otter; Air Niugini no longer flies there; yam festival June or July; 'Flights out can be cancelled. Don't leave it until the last minute' if you have connections.

Louisiade Archipelago: very few tourists apart from yachts; airfield on Misima (Bwagoia) served by small aircraft from the mainland; most visitors arrive by private yacht from Cairns (about 510 nautical miles, about 4 days). Local transport is canoe or open longboat, 'only be recommended to the extremely adventurous'; Misima to other islands crosses open ocean with no way to signal distress. Its 'Stay safe' section is empty.

Diving: Wikivoyage's Alotau page says 'The diving is reportedly fantastic but Alotau gets few visitors and the one dive shop has closed down for lack of customers.' Wikipedia/Wikivoyage Milne Bay describe the reefs as among the most biodiverse; Tawali dive resort is not mentioned on either Alotau page.

Safety: the Alotau page has no safety section or warning; it says the town is 'Far from the violence of PNG's capital, Port Moresby' and that 'the people are very friendly'. Country-wide PNG safety (Stay safe section): crime gangs concentrated in Port Moresby and Lae; avoid going out after dark; saltwater crocodiles common in coastal waters ('Avoid swimming except at higher elevations and in hotel swimming pools'); malaria a hazard; small-plane flying risky; January 2024 US advisory quoted: 'Reconsider travel to Papua New Guinea due to crime, civil unrest, and piracy' (do-not-travel areas: central Bougainville and the Highlands except Mt Hagen and Goroka; Milne Bay not named).

Climate: tropical rainforest (Köppen Af) with heavy rainfall year-round, annual rainfall about 3,055-3,108 mm. Monthly rainfall (Wikipedia table, mm): Jan 163, Feb 179, Mar 186, Apr 285, May 369, Jun 341, Jul 308, Aug 291, Sep 346, Oct 282, Nov 164, Dec 141. So Nov to Mar is the least rainy, May and Sep the wettest.

PNG-wide: 'The (very) wet season runs from about December to March.' This conflicts with the Alotau station figures above (Dec lowest), so the south-east does not follow the national pattern; do not apply the national wet-season statement to Alotau.

Betel nut is widely chewed in Alotau and Milne Bay; the red spit stains the ground. Fresh food at Alotau market: bananas, sweet potatoes, yams, greens, seafood including crabs; fresh most of the week, 'except Saturday afternoon and Sunday'.

Louisiades etiquette: almost everything is privately owned, even fish in the lagoon; get permission before fishing or taking anything; trade goods (fish hooks, line, sugar, batteries, soap, etc.) are welcomed.

tips.fact: Accommodation near Alotau (undated Wikivoyage prices): Driftwood Resort K300 per bungalow; Bibiko Farm K60 with food; Alotau International Hotel +675 641 0300; Doini Island Plantation Resort about one hour by boat.
Do not leave island flights to the last minute; they can be cancelled.
Islands beyond Alotau have very limited accommodation (Normanby, Goodenough) and no regular passenger ferry; arrange boat and lodging in advance.
Handshake greeting matters; do not photograph people without consent.

research.events: Trobriand yam festival June or July (Trobriand page); not shown to drive crowds at Alotau itself.
unverified: Tawali dive resort area: neither Alotau nor Milne Bay Wikivoyage mentions Tawali; no operator page, prices, season or access method fetched.
Diving seasons (calm/best months): not stated in any fetched source. Only monthly rainfall is sourced.
